source_classification.source_derived: Statements reproduced or conservatively constrained from the cited sources without adding a clinical threshold or converting evidence grades into probabilities.
source_classification.proposed_for_review: Agent-proposed graph, states, transforms, horizons, wording, and reference values; not source-derived clinical rules.
source_classification.drafting_lead: BN-13 is an incomplete, inference-disabled and deployment-disabled drafting lead, not an approved mapping. Its seven deterministic 0/1 review tables were replaced with soft argmax-preserving placeholders; no BN-13 activation metadata was copied.

question_enumeration.specific_question: For an adult follow-up encounter whose akathisia effect status is recorded as present, given current restlessness severity, observed motor restlessness, diagnostic/attribution context, regimen-change feasibility and tradeoff, adjunct safety-review context, and urgent concern, what is the posterior distribution over option-discussion prompts (regimen review vs adjunct review vs both vs constrained discussion vs establish-indication-first), with parallel indication and urgent-safety review prompts, to structure physician review?
question_enumeration.intended_setting: Adult outpatient follow-up for schizophrenia; current dated encounter. Not the emergency department. Local setting confirmation requested.
question_enumeration.proposed_time_horizon: Current encounter (no outcome prediction horizon). The 4-week onset lookback and medication-change history are constituents of the proposed attribution field, not a timed prediction.

output_meanings.established_current_association: Review prompt: akathisia associated with antipsychotic exposure is recorded; option discussion may proceed. Not a diagnosis and not a prescription.
output_meanings.assess_differential_and_association: Review prompt: attribution is alternative-or-unresolved or partly unknown; work up onset timing, medication review, and exclusions before any option discussion. No option prompt from this branch.
output_meanings.no_current_treatment_rule: Review prompt: attribution and movement observation are both still unknown; there is no basis for even a differential workup prompt beyond routine assessment. Not a negative finding.
output_meanings.review_regimen_and_adjunct: Review prompt: indication established, regimen changes reviewable, adjunct safety routine; discuss all four source options with tradeoff monitoring. Not a prescription, product choice, or dose.
output_meanings.review_regimen_options: Review prompt: indication established with regimen reviewable but adjunct safety heightened or unknown; lead with dose-reduction/switch discussion and complete adjunct safety review first.
output_meanings.review_adjunct_options: Review prompt: indication established with routine adjunct safety but constrained or unknown regimen feasibility; lead with benzodiazepine/beta-blocker discussion with patient-preference elicitation and continued psychosis monitoring.
output_meanings.review_constrained_options: Review prompt: indication established but both pathways carry constraints or unknown safety; discuss all options with explicit benefit-harm balancing, adherence assessment, and preference elicitation.
output_meanings.establish_indication_first: Review prompt: attribution unresolved; establish indication before any option discussion.
output_meanings.urgent_clinician_assessment: Parallel prompt plus deterministic flag: recorded suicidality, dysphoria, or other urgent concern takes priority regardless of diagnostic status.

source_comparison.bn13_scope_vs_f2: BN-13 is a 20-node review-workflow draft (13 clinician inputs with missing priors + 7 deterministic 0/1 review outputs) with inference_allowed=false and deployment_allowed=false. F2 keeps its input vocabulary (severity, observed movements, association, dose/switch feasibility, psychosis tradeoff, preference, urgent/distress-adherence, benzo and propranolol safety) and its parallel-review structure (indication, options, urgent) but restructures them into a 9-node executable network: 6 roots + 3 outputs with 3 GIVEN edges. Dose and switch feasibility plus psychosis tradeoff are assessed together in one RegimenFeasibility field; the five adjunct safety concerns are assessed per-class in one field aggregated to a 3-state AdjunctSafetyContext node; preference and distress/adherence detail remain template-rendered discussion items rather than nodes in v0.1. All seven BN-13 deterministic 0/1 tables were replaced with soft argmax-preserving synthetic placeholders; no BN-13 TABLE bytes, priors, or inference/deployment flags were copied.
source_comparison.bars_use_and_non_rule: The BARS global anchors 2-5 supply the four severity labels; the objective/awareness/distress items supply the observation and interview constituents of the proposed motor and attribution fields. The 0-9 component total is explicitly excluded from every mapping (recorded as descriptive only per the source), and no BARS item score is a network state. Recording the severity labels does not require administering every BARS item and does not establish medication causation.
source_comparison.severity_reuse: The mild/moderate/marked/severe enum follows the history-effects draft proposal (itself reproducing BARS global labels), which remains awaiting_review and therefore unapproved; F2 treats it as a candidate mapping and flags the approval dependency in Q1. Observed motor restlessness is kept distinct from subjective severity per the criteria source (global 2 assignable with fidgeting only; pseudoakathisia rule).
source_comparison.guideline_gives_no_decision_rule: STATEMENT-13 states a 2C suggestion of four options with explicit benefit-harm balancing and per-patient preferences, no dose selection, no product ranking, and an explicit electronic-decision-support restriction. The 5-state OptionReview preserves those options as discussion prompts only; the posterior maximum is never a prescription rule, and the CDSS restriction is resolved by review-prompts-only framing plus a deterministic urgent flag that does not decide treatment.
source_comparison.history_reuse: FR-21 status/severity mechanics are reused as the gate plus RestlessnessSeverity mapping; the history draft's mapping gaps (unresolved-vs-not_assessed, effect-specific inputs) are resolved here by separate proposed AttributionContext/MotorRestlessness/RegimenFeasibility/AdjunctSafetyContext/UrgentConcern fields, each unknown-permitting except the two required inputs.

nodes: IndicationReview (3 states; parents in order AttributionContext, MotorRestlessness)
OptionReview (5 states; parents in order IndicationReview, RegimenFeasibility, AdjunctSafetyContext)
graph_decision.why_this_shape: One indication review node over the two diagnostic inputs plus one option-discussion node over indication, regimen feasibility, and adjunct safety, plus one parallel urgent node, mirroring BN-13's parallel-output structure at an executable size (184 cells). Dose/product selection, propranolol/benzodiazepine dosing, and candidate-specific safety screening stay outside the network as physician label review; they remain visible as template context wording and owner questions. All discrete nature nodes for the v1 execution profile; no latent nodes, no posterior chaining into other questions.
graph_decision.double_counting_rationale_for_review: Each assessed input is proposed as usage=both (CPT-estimation context + hard observation). Rationale for review: conditioning once in Bayes rule is a single update, not double counting; the LLM conditions table estimates on the patient's context while inference instantiates the same observed states as evidence. Optional missing inputs use estimation context only (the gap is noted in the conditioning context) with no hard evidence, so no update occurs on an unobserved node. Owner to accept or restrict any mapping to observation-only.

Indication rows from the documented mapping: associated -> established [0.82,0.09,0.09] (3 rows); alternative -> assess [0.09,0.82,0.09] (3 rows); unknown with observed present/absent -> assess (2 rows); unknown with unknown movements -> no_rule [0.09,0.09,0.82] (1 row). Option rows: non-established indication -> establish [0.045 x4, 0.82] (18 rows); established + feasible + routine -> both [0.82, 0.045 x4] (1 row); established + feasible + heightened/unknown -> regimen_options (2 rows); established + constrained/unknown + routine -> adjunct_options (2 rows); established + constrained/unknown + heightened/unknown -> constrained_options (4 rows). Urgent: present [0.90,0.10], absent [0.10,0.90]. Lookup exists only to give the validator/inference harness complete, normalized, correctly ordered tables. Never present these as patient estimates.

unresolved_assumptions: The severity enum and all six akathisia_assessment fields are proposals; the history-effects package itself is still awaiting_review, so no severity definition used here is approved.
The 4-week onset window, EPS-treatment-reduction trigger, and antiemetic/antidepressant review scope are constituents of the attribution field, not encoded gates or probabilities.
Propranolol dosing, benzodiazepine product choice, mirtazapine use, and candidate-specific safety screening are physician-side review items in v0.1, not network nodes.
The adjunct aggregate node preserves per-class detail only in the field and template disclosure; per-class estimation separation needs review.
Reference tables are synthetic placeholders with zero clinical validity.
